name: Bena (Nigeria)
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress

earlier_scan.note: Only classification/tone-reconstruction work (Kleinewillinghöfer; Idiatov & Van de Velde); Wikipedia notes 3-tone system, no stress statement, no grammar

sources.citation: Idiatov, Dmitry. 2023. Neutralization of laryngeal settings of word-final stops in Buto languages. Slides, 2nd Adamawa Conference, Paris.
sources.note: Nothing on stress; segmental (coda laryngeal neutralization).

sources.citation: Idiatov, Dmitry & Mark Van de Velde. 2020. The internal reconstruction of Bena-Yungur consonants and tone patterns. Language in Africa 1(3): 100-124. DOI 10.37892/2686-8946-2020-1-3-100-124 (HAL halshs-03088857)
sources.note: Nothing on stress; historical/internal reconstruction of the H/M/L tone system from a two-tone system via stem-initial depressor consonants, and of lexical tone patterns; no mention of stress or accent.

sources.citation: Kleinewillinghöfer, Ulrich. 2020. Adamawa. In Rainer Vossen & Gerrit J. Dimmendaal (eds.), The Oxford Handbook of African Languages, 220-230. Oxford: OUP.
sources.note: Family overview cited on the AdaGram Bena page; may contain a general statement on prosody (tone vs. stress) in Bena-Mboi/Adamawa languages, second-hand at best.

sources.citation: Idiatov, Dmitry & Mark Van de Velde. 2019. Bena-Mboi is Benue-Congo. Slides, Adamawa Conference, Mainz, 11 Sept 2019.
Idiatov, Dmitry & Mark Van de Velde. 2019. Tonal reconstruction of Bena-Yungur: depressor consonants and directionality of tonal interactions. Slides, Adamawa Conference, Mainz, 9 Sept 2019.

Idiatov, Dmitry. 2019. Word-final consonant epenthesis in North-eastern Nigerian English. English Language and Linguistics 23(2): 303-340. DOI 10.1017/S1360674317000429 (copy on AdaGram project site; describes Bena English with reference to Bena L1 phonetics)
sources.note: Mentions stress only for English words in Bena speakers' L2 English (e.g. [ŋ] retention in stressed syllables); says nothing about stress in Bena-Yungur L1.

sources.citation: Idiatov, Dmitry & Mark Van de Velde. 2018. The tone system of Bena-Yungur. In Raija Kramer & Roland Kießling (eds.), Current approaches to Adamawa and Gur languages, 171-191. Cologne: Rüdiger Köppe. (publisher-paginated final version from author's site; HAL author version halshs-02052863 also saved)
sources.note: Nothing. §2 'Grammatical overview' (pp.172-173) gives consonant/vowel inventories, contrastive vowel length, syllable structure, final-vowel reduction; §§3-5 describe a three-level tone system (H, M, L), tone spread/absorption/floating tones and tonal morphology. The words stress/accent do not occur (only 'prominent' once, about tone spread in the Guto dialect).

sources.citation: Van de Velde, Mark & Dmitry Idiatov. 2017. Morphological classes and gender in Ɓə́ná-Yungur. In Shigeki Kaji (ed.), Proceedings of the 8th World Congress of African Linguistics, 53-65. Tokyo: ILCAA, Tokyo University of Foreign Studies. (HAL halshs-01484016)
sources.access_detail: a digital copy (available on request); access check: not located online or in the libraries checked
sources.note: Nothing; noun-class/gender morphology paper, no stress/accent mention.

sources.citation: Kleinewillinghöfer, Ulrich. 2011/2015. Ɓəna-Mboi (Yungur) Group: overview, pronouns and numbers, 100-word comparative list, noun-class evidence. Adamawa Language Projects, JGU Mainz (web page + linked PDFs).
sources.note: Overview page read; wordlists only, no prosodic description (linked wordlist PDFs not downloaded).

sources.citation: AdaGram project, Bena-Yungur language page (Idiatov & Van de Velde),https://llacan.cnrs.fr/AdaGram/bena-yungur.html
sources.note: Nothing; states that 'an overview of basic phonology and morphosyntax of Bena-Yungur can be found in Van de Velde & Idiatov (2017) and Idiatov & Van de Velde (2018)' and lists the Bena-English dictionary app (2021/2024).

sources.citation: Idiatov, Dmitry, Mark L.O. Van de Velde & Uyên-To Rabier (programmer). 2021/2024. Bena-English dictionary, versions 1.0/2.0 (Android app),https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=com.efl.bena
